Poland confirms brief drone incursion on 23 November

23 November 2026 · Lubelskie · confirmed brief drone incursion

Polish Operational Command confirmed one brief drone entry and later exit

Poland’s Operational Command confirmed that one drone briefly entered Polish airspace on the evening of 23 November during Russian strikes on western Ukraine. The military attributed the drone to Russia.

Operational Command spokesperson Lt Col Jacek Goryszewski said the object left Polish airspace without weapons being used. The exact crossing location and timing, model, payload and intended target are unknown. The map marker shows a broad Lubelskie warning-area reference, not a flight path.

The Government Security Centre issued a readiness advisory, followed by a wider shelter warning and an all-clear before midnight. These warnings are part of the same occurrence. This entry is distinct from the 20 November breach and does not establish an attack on Poland.

Attribution and uncertainty

Polish Operational Command attributed the drone to Russia. Operator details, intended target and reason for entry were not independently established.
Investigation / uncertainty
No published precise track, exact duration, model, payload or intended target in the reviewed sources. Public warning and all-clear times do not establish a crossing or exit time.
